Question: If Fox news is according to the left, such a discredited news source, how do you explain how they beat CNN and MSNBC in ratings for so many years in a row?
Answer: Congratulations, your logical fallacy is argumentum ad populum! Argumentum ad populum, also known as “appeal to popularity,” is any argument that states that, just because many people like (or dislike, or believe) something, it must be good (or bad, or true). This is a common fallacy often found in advertising, insisting that a brand must be good because it is the most popular. This also pops up in politics, where people insist that a law or policy must be good because the majority of people support it. The flaw in the argument is that the majority of people can be wrong. For instance, during the Civil Rights movement in the 1960s, the majority of Americans still believed that Jim Crow laws were morally acceptable, despite history showing this not to be the case. With the specific examples of Fox News, the reason it has such a high viewership is that it is the only mainstream news outlet with a specifically conservative bias. When people want non-biased news reporting they have a lot of options: CNN, network news stations like NBC, CBS, ABC, etc, NPR, BBC, etc. This means that the number or people seeking out this type of news is going to be split up among multiple channels, while the conservative audience is going to be primarily concentrated on Fox News. The ratings have nothing to do with the journalistic integrity of the channel, however. It's merely a reflection of Fox News' market dominance of the conservative news audience.

Question: Why did historic people abandon bronze in making tools and weapons and adopt iron instead?
Answer: Iron ore is much more common than copper and tin ores, the components of bronze. Refined iron is also harder and more durable than bronze, meaning that iron tools and weapons will last longer, break less frequently, and hold their shape and sharpness longer than bronze ones. The main reason bronze was used predominantly in antiquity was because the components of bronze have a much lower melting point than iron. Iron's melting point at sea level is 1,538°C (2,800°F), whereas the melting points of copper and tin are 1,085°C (1,984°F) and 232°C (450°F) respectively. Early metallurgists didn't have the technology to get their smelters hot enough to refine iron ore but could get them hot enough to smelt bronze. Once the technology advanced enough to allow iron smelting most metallurgists switched to the stronger and more abundant metal.

Question: How do I get cornmeal to stick to fish?
Answer: You need to get the fish wet. I usually whip up an egg or two (or more, depending on the size of the fish), then dip the fish into the whipped egg before dipping it into the breading (I use Panko breadcrumbs, but others use cornmeal or flower). The breading will stick to the egg and it will add some extra flavor to the food. If you don't like/can't eat egg you can dip the fish in heavy cream or brush it with oil before adding the breading. Basically you just need something for the cornmeal to stick to. Don't use water, though, especially if you're frying the fish in hot oil. Water and oil don't mix, so as the water heats and boils it will form bubbles that can splash oil around, potentially causing burns or creating a fire. Hope that helps!

Question: Are clouds and steam just tiny water droplets? If so, should they have the same density as water, which is much heavier than air, and should sink to the ground fast? Why are they not sinking?
Answer: Clouds and steam are not drops of water, they are water vapor, which is water molecules in gaseous form. Water vapor is less dense than oxygen and nitrogen gasses, the two main components of the atmosphere, and thus rises upwards. Large amounts of atmospheric water vapor form clouds. When the vapor cools and condenses, it forms water droplets which are liquid and thus denser than the atmospheric gasses. These drops fall to the ground as rain.
